| L39 | 2026-07-13 | When a bracket-ladder P&L is a **small net of two large legs** (Σ collected premium ≈ the \$1 payout — S14's mean +\$0.0925 sits on top of a ~\$0.51–\$0.97 winner-\$1 loss), a **candlestick/volume fill proxy** (`high ≥ ask AND volume > 0`) that credits the **income leg without queue position is biased UPWARD**: a bar only proves the price *printed*, not that a resting offer ahead of the whole book would have filled. The loss leg is NOT so biased (heavy volume sweeps the offer — S14 winner filled 96.7%), so the bias is **asymmetric** and inflates the net. A per-leg **volume gate** (require the income leg to carry volume ≥ X) is **necessary-but-INSUFFICIENT** — it caps thin-print optimism but cannot model the **adverse-selection correlation** between *which* income strikes fill and *which* strike wins (which the queue-blind proxy assumes independent). Before claiming fillability, **decompose the edge as a fraction of the thinnest income legs**: S14's \$0.072 of \$0.093 (**78%**) came from sub-100-contract-volume legs, and the "complete fill" gate term was exactly \$0 (0.0% complete-fill) — the fat nominal overround never underwrites; the edge is entirely near-money partial pass-through.
